headline: Two meters: Active CPU at $0.128 per vCPU-hour (only while code runs, I/O wait excluded) and provisioned memory at $0.0212 per GB-hour for the whole session wall clock, with a one-minute minimum on memory only. There is no published CPU minimum. Hobby is a capped free allowance with a 45-minute session limit; Pro is a $20 platform fee that returns $20 of credit and a 24-hour session limit.

included.notes: Unit allowances, not dollars: 5 Active-CPU hours, 420 GB-hours of provisioned memory, 5,000 sandbox creations, 20 GB data transfer per month, plus 15 GB of snapshot storage and 15 GB of drive storage for the lifetime of the account. Hard stop: no overage.

compute.cpuBasis: active use only: Active CPU counts the CPU time your code actually consumes, summed across the sandbox's vCPUs. Time waiting on I/O, database queries or model calls is not billed.
compute.ramBasis: allocated: provisioned memory is the memory allocated to the sandbox multiplied by the time the session runs, including idle time.
compute.billingIncrement: Provisioned memory is billed in 1-minute minimum increments. No CPU metering interval is published.
compute.minimum: A 1-minute minimum applies to provisioned memory per session. No minimum is published for Active CPU; only memory is described as having one.

rates.quote: The amount of time your code actively uses the CPU, measured in hours. Time spent waiting for I/O (such as network requests, database queries, or AI model calls) does not count toward Active CPU.
Provisioned memory is billed in 1 minute minimum increments to account for sandbox lifecycle management.
You can provision 1 or an even number of vCPUs between 2 and 32 depending on your plan. The default is 2 vCPUs.
Each vCPU includes 2 GB of memory.

hermesAgent.status: official Vercel guide for the Hermes Vercel Sandbox terminal backend
hermesAgent.oneClickOrManaged: no one-click deploy; a step-by-step guide that still runs Hermes on your own machine
hermesAgent.summary: Vercel documents Hermes as a terminal backend: you install Hermes locally, point terminal.backend at vercel_sandbox, authenticate with Vercel, and the agent's commands run in a Sandbox microVM. Hermes itself is not hosted by Vercel, so this is not an always-on agent deployment. The guide requires macOS, Linux or Windows with WSL2, Hermes 0.20.0+, and the Vercel CLI linked to a project.
steps: Install Hermes with the official installer (or `hermes update` to 0.20.0+).
`hermes config set terminal.backend vercel_sandbox`, set terminal.vercel_runtime (node24/node22/python3.13), and set container_cpu with container_memory = 2,048 x CPU.
Authenticate: `vercel env pull` and export VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN for local use, or set VERCEL_TOKEN, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID and VERCEL_TEAM_ID for long-running processes.
Run `hermes doctor`, then `hermes`; commands execute in a Sandbox as the vercel-sandbox user with /vercel/sandbox as the workspace root.
hermesAgent.nonCoderDashboard: No. It needs a terminal, a Vercel project link and environment variables; the sandbox is created by the Hermes process, not from the dashboard.
hermesAgent.alwaysOn: No. One sandbox per task, recreated as needed, with filesystem snapshots between tasks; live processes do not survive.

evidence.quote: Its Vercel Sandbox terminal backend runs every command the agent executes inside an isolated Vercel Sandbox microVM instead of on your machine.
One sandbox per task: Hermes creates a sandbox on demand when the agent first runs a terminal command and reuses it for the rest of the task.
Live processes do not survive sandbox recreation.
macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL2

openClaw.status: official Vercel Knowledge Base guide plus a Vercel Labs proof-of-concept repository
openClaw.oneClickOrManaged: no one-click deploy; a manual CLI walkthrough (Sandbox CLI, npm, onboarding wizard, QR pairing)
openClaw.summary: Vercel's KB walks through running OpenClaw inside a Vercel Sandbox: create a sandbox with a published port and a timeout, install OpenClaw globally, run the onboarding wizard, start the gateway with nohup, pair the browser, and link WhatsApp by QR. The gateway is reachable at the sandbox's public HTTPS URL. The vercel-labs/vercel-openclaw repo is a separate review PoC for a Slack-driven warm/sleep lifecycle and is explicitly not production-ready.
steps: `sandbox create --timeout 30m --publish-port 18789 --connect`; note the sandbox ID and public URL.
`npm install -g openclaw`, then `openclaw onboard` (model provider, API key, skip channels).
Start the gateway in the background with nohup so it survives disconnect; open the dashboard at the public URL with the token fragment.
Approve the browser with `openclaw devices list` / `openclaw devices approve`, then link WhatsApp by QR and restart the gateway.
Optionally snapshot the sandbox after install and lock egress to an allowlist with `sandbox config network-policy`.
openClaw.nonCoderDashboard: No. Every step is a terminal command; the OpenClaw dashboard only becomes usable after the CLI onboarding and device approval.
openClaw.alwaysOn: Only up to the session timeout: the guide uses a 30-minute timeout and notes that sandboxes shut down when it expires. The KB frames this as keeping the assistant reachable without a laptop, not as an indefinite host.

evidence.quote: A Vercel Sandbox gives OpenClaw its own isolated Linux MicroVM, completely separate from your local machine.
Timeouts: sandboxes shut down automatically when the timeout expires, so nothing runs forever by accident
This is a review PoC, not a production-ready hosting service.

deploy.alwaysOnVerdict: Weakest of the three for an always-on personal agent. Sessions cap at 24 hours on Pro (45 minutes on Hobby), a sandbox only resumes when something calls it, and live processes do not survive a stop. The official guides are for a laptop-driven agent whose commands run in a sandbox, not for hosting the agent itself.

notVerified: No Vercel account or sandbox was created; all behaviour is from documentation.
CPU metering granularity is not published; only the memory minimum is.
Per-region rates other than iad1 were not read from the interactive selector.
Whether a sandbox port can be attached to a customer's own domain was not confirmed.
